extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators (applicants) and host institutions preparing ERC frontier research grant proposals under Horizon 2020
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/evaluation rules for preparing and submitting ERC Starting, Consolidator, Advanced and Proof of Concept grant proposals under the ERC Work Programme 2014. Covers eligibility, PI profiles, host-institution obligations, funding rules, ethics, research integrity and peer-review evaluation criteria and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence as sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion on the basis of which ERC frontier research grants are awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is conducted by peer-review panels of renowned scientists (possibly assisted by remote referees). The process is designed to identify scientific excellence irrespective of gender, age, nationality or institution and to take career breaks and unconventional career paths into account. Emphasis on frontier research, interdisciplinary and pioneering/unconventional approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria: Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the objectives of the proposed project consistent with the requirements specified in the work programme and/or call for proposals? Do they, where appropriate, correspond to, or go beyond, best current practice?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by panels as part of the peer review. Marked on a 0–5 scale. Panels expect ground-breaking nature, ambition and feasibility; proposals should address frontiers of knowledge and be inspirational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the project have a substantial impact in the context of the ERC strategic objectives?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed on a 0–5 scale. Impact should be framed relative to ERC objectives (advances at frontiers of knowledge); arguments about potential scientific, societal, economic or disciplinary impact are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria: Quality and efficiency of implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed methodology and work plan effective in reaching the goals of the project? Do they ensure the highest quality and/or utility of results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed on a 0–5 scale. Panels evaluate clarity, feasibility, methodology, workpackages, milestones, management, risk mitigation and resource justification. Overall quality threshold of 80% applied to establish retained list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Each evaluation criterion is scored on a scale of 0 to 5; an overall quality threshold of 80% is used to establish the retained list of proposals which will be ranked in order of priority for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels combine criterion scores per the call's rules to decide retained list and ranking. Panels must explain suggested budget modifications in writing if they propose changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal completeness and scope eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must be complete and submitted before the relevant call deadline; a complete proposal entails all requested parts or sections. The content must relate to the objectives and to the grant type set out in the call; a proposal will be deemed ineligible on grounds of scope only in clear-cut cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete proposals may be declared ineligible. Where doubt exists, evaluation may proceed pending eligibility review committee decision; if eligibility criteria are not met at any point the proposal will be declared ineligible and not considered further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible scientific fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be made in any field of research (with the exception of research within scope of Annex I to the Euratom Treaty, which must be submitted to Euratom calls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERC operates bottom-up without predetermined priorities; encourages interdisciplinary and cross-boundary proposals. Applicants should select the appropriate ERC panel/primary panel structure (Annex 1) matching their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Principal Investigator: nationality/residence/role
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC actions are open to researchers of any nationality who may reside in any country at time of application. Starting, Consolidator and Advanced proposals are submitted by the Principal Investigator who has scientific responsibility for the project, on behalf of the host institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs may be of any age and need not be based full-time in Europe; specific grant profiles impose additional requirements (see PI profile entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting Grant PI eligibility (time-since-PhD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator shall have been awarded their first PhD at least 2 and up to 7 years prior to the publication date of the Starting Grant call (effective elapsed time may be reduced in properly documented circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elapsed time reductions apply for maternity (18 months per child), paternity (actual leave taken), long-term illness, clinical training or national service (actual leave taken). Elapsed time must not surpass 11 years 6 months after adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidator Grant PI eligibility (time-since-PhD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigator shall have been awarded their first PhD over 7 and up to 12 years prior to the publication date of the Consolidator Grant call (effective elapsed time may be reduced in properly documented circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same reduction rules apply as for Starting Grants; elapsed time must not surpass 16 years 6 months after adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant PI eligibility (no time-since-PhD limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grants have no specific time-since-PhD eligibility criterion; applicants are expected to be established research leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators expect a record of significant achievements in the last 10 years; absence of such a record makes success unlikely.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI track record / early achievements evidence (Starting and Consolidator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate potential for independence and evidence of maturity: Starting applicants expected to have produced at least one important publication without their PhD supervisor; Consolidator applicants expected to have produced several important publications without their PhD supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should list representative publications (Starting: highlight five; Consolidator: highlight ten), number of citations (excluding self-citations), granted patents (if applicable), invited presentations, prizes and awards (if applicable). These items form part of the evaluation of the PI's track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Grant track-record benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced Grant PIs should demonstrate significant research achievements in the last 10 years, matching benchmarks such as: 10 senior-author publications in major journals; or 3 major research monographs (one translated); or combinations/alternatives (5 patents, 10 invited presentations, leadership in expeditions/conferences, prizes, major contributions to launching careers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks are indicative and may be considered individually or combined to evidence exceptional leadership, originality and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI time commitment requirements (Starting & Consolidator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators funded through the ERC Starting and Consolidator Grants shall spend a minimum 50% of their total working time on the ERC project and a minimum of 50% of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs must ensure sufficient time commitment and presence throughout the project to guarantee proper execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution eligibility and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institution (applicant legal entity) must engage the Principal Investigator for at least the duration of the project and must be established in an EU Member State or Associated Country, or be an eligible international/EU organisation. Institutions must provide conditions enabling the PI to independently direct research and manage its funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions (subject to supplementary agreement) must ensure the PI can apply for funding independently; manage research and funding and allocate resources; publish independently as senior author; supervise team members (including doctoral students); and have access to appropriate space and facilities. These conditions should be consistent with the European Charter for Researchers and Code of Conduct for Recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution and project participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution is expected to be the only participating legal entity; additional team members may be hosted by additional legal entities if they bring scientific added value and may be located anywhere (including outside EU) if essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortia agreements are not required for ERC multi-beneficiary grants. Legal entities outside EU/Associated Countries are eligible for funding only when participation is essential; see Annex 3 for restrictions on some third-country entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on submissions and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Principal Investigator may submit only one proposal to the ERC for frontier research grant calls under the same Work Programme. Researchers may participate as PI or Co-Investigator in only one ERC frontier research project at any one time. PIs with an existing ERC frontier research project may not submit another proposal unless the existing project ends no more than two years after the call deadline. Panel members serving in specified years may be restricted from applying in the same year/type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals evaluated as category C in a given Work Programme may be barred from submitting in subsequent specified years (e.g., category C in 2014 barred from 2015 & 2016); category B may be barred from the following year (details in restrictions section). Ineligible or withdrawn proposals do not count against restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts and additional one-off costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum grant varies by type: Starting up to EUR 1,500,000 (plus up to EUR 500,000 extra for start-up/equipment/access); Consolidator up to EUR 2,000,000 (plus up to EUR 750,000); Advanced up to EUR 2,500,000 (plus up to EUR 1,000,000). Proof of Concept has separate budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional funding requested must cover eligible start-up costs (for PIs moving to EU/Associated Countries), purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities. Additional one-off funds are not pro-rata reduced for shorter projects; all funding requested is assessed during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification and Union contribution rules
rubrics_metrics.description: During peer review, panels will assess the funding requested by the applicant against the needs of the project; funding requested must be fully justified by an estimation of the real project cost. Union contribution reimburses up to 100% of total eligible approved direct costs plus flat-rate financing of indirect costs at 25% of total eligible direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels may suggest modifications to the indicative budgetary breakdown where requests are not properly justified and must explain such suggested modifications in writing. The awarded grant level is a maximum figure; final paid amount must be justified on actual costs incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and data sharing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC supports open access to published outputs (peer-reviewed articles, monographs, data and data-related products such as computer codes). The ERC Model Grant Agreement will address how publications must be made available through open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERC considers deposition of data and data-related products in relevant databases essential and recommends deposition as soon as possible, although data deposition is not a formal requirement of the Grant Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical principles and civil-application focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research shall comply with ethical principles and relevant national, Union and international legislation, including EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and ECHR; attention to proportionality, privacy, personal data protection, physical/mental integrity, non-discrimination and high levels of human health protection. Research must have exclusive focus on civil applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding of human embryonic stem cell research is possible within Horizon 2020's ethical framework; applicants must ensure compliance and address ethical issues in proposal sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity and misconduct sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and promote a culture of research integrity at all stages; cases of fabrication, falsification, plagiarism or misrepresentation of data arising during evaluation or project life-cycle will be addressed vigorously and may be sanctioned (exclusion of proposals, requests to host institutions, suspension or termination of grants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions bear primary responsibility for detection, investigation and adjudication of misconduct and must have structures in place; host institutions expected to verify and notify ERC of pending allegations. ERC enforces confidentiality and conflict-of-interest rules in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review panels and evaluation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation is conducted by peer review panels composed of renowned scientists and scholars selected by the ERC Scientific Council; panels may be assisted by remote referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are monitored to guarantee transparency, fairness and impartiality; evaluations should take career breaks and unconventional careers into account. Proposals are allocated to panels/panels' subdomains per Annex 1; cross-/multi-disciplinary proposals are evaluated by regular panels with appropriate external expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel/panel-structure assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC uses a primary panel structure across three main research domains (Physical Sciences & Engineering; Life Sciences; Social Sciences & Humanities) with individual panels PE1–PE10, LS1–LS9, SH1–SH6 for field assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must choose the appropriate panel reflecting their proposal's scientific domain; indicative budgets are allocated per domain (Physical 44%, Life 39%, SSH 17%) and then to panels proportional to demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD equivalence and degree-date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Starting or Consolidator Grants a PI must have been awarded a PhD or equivalent doctoral degree; first-professional degrees are not considered PhD-equivalent. For medical doctors, an MD alone is not accepted as PhD-equivalent unless accompanied by additional research credentials or a PhD; date rules apply to calculate eligibility windows (e.g., MD+2 years reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance points to EURYDICE and NSF lists for recognized doctoral titles. For MD holders without PhD, certified date of MD completion plus two years is the time reference for eligibility-window calculations; for holders of both MD and PhD the earliest qualifying degree date applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions and sanctions related to prior evaluations and panel membership
rubrics_metrics.description: A PI whose proposal was evaluated as category C in specified Work Programmes may be barred from submitting proposals in subsequent specified years; PIs serving as Panel Members in specified years may be restricted from applying for the same type of grant in those years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions aim to maintain evaluation quality and allow unsuccessful applicants time to strengthen proposals. Specific bans (e.g., category C in 2014 barred for 2015/2016) are listed in the work programme and may be updated by the Scientific Council.
